CalFresh — Alameda County Social Services Agency (via archived official page, captured January 2025)

CalFresh is a nutrition assistance program that helps individuals and families buy healthy food. Benefits are issued on an Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) card, which works like a debit card at most grocery stores and farmers markets, and some restaurants. The EBT card is also issued for cash aid (CalWORKs, General Assistance, Refugee Cash Assistance); EBT customer service: 1-877-328-9677. Changes in household situation affecting benefits must be reported within 10 days.

Eligibility is based on income, California residency, assets, household size, immigration status, employment status, and age. Income guidelines (July 1, 2024 – June 30, 2025): 1 person $2,430/month; 2 persons $3,288; 3 persons $4,144; 4 persons $5,002; 5 persons $5,858; 6 persons $6,716; 7 persons $7,574; 8 persons $8,430; add $858 per additional person. CalWORKs recipients are also eligible for CalFresh. Special rules exist for students, elderly/disabled applicants (ESAP), and homeless households.

How to apply: online at BenefitsCal.com; complete form CF 285 and return it in person or by mail to any agency office; or call (510) 263-2420 or (888) 999-4772 to have an application mailed. Include: completed application, copy of photo ID, proof of income, proof of residency. EBT cards are issued within 30 days of application (3 days for expedited service). To keep benefits: complete a semi-annual SAR 7 report, annual recertification with interview, and report mid-year changes (income over the reporting threshold; lottery/gambling winnings of $3,750+ from a single game) within 10 days.

Customer Service Call Center: (510) 263-2420 or (888) 999-4772, Monday–Friday 7:30 a.m.–5:15 p.m. Offices open Monday–Friday 8:30 a.m.–5:00 p.m. except County holidays.
